articles.title: India snub hit hard, but Suryakumar Yadav is rediscovering love, passion for cricket - India Today
articles.summary: India snub hit hard, but Suryakumar Yadav is rediscovering love, passion for cricket India Today
articles.content: Being dropped from the team you once led is never easy. Finding the motivation to pick yourself up and fight your way back can be even harder. For Suryakumar Yadav, the blow was particularly painful. He had captained India to a successful T20 World Cup title defence, only to find himself out of the national setup a few months later.A prolonged lean patch with the bat eventually cost him his place in the side. The BCCI decided to move on from the former skipper ahead of the England tour, with Shreyas Iyer taking over the leadership responsibilities.The fall from being at the helm of a World Cup-winning side to watching from the sidelines took its toll. But Suryakumar is now beginning to find his feet again, rediscovering the love and passion that first drew him towards the game.Speaking to the media at a T20 Mumbai League Celebrating the Champions event, as quoted by PTI, the former India captain admitted that the period following India's World Cup triumph had been particularly challenging."Post the T20 World Cup win it has been a little difficult. I don't want to run away from that fact. If you are not honest with yourself, it is very difficult to lead a happy life," Suryakumar said during a T20 Mumbai League Celebrating the Champions event here.However, life away from the cricket field brought him a new source of happiness. Suryakumar revealed that becoming a father earlier this year helped him shift his attention away from the disappointment of losing his place in the Indian team."To be very honest, it (not being part of the team) has been very difficult. But at the same time, during the IPL, I was blessed with a baby girl in May. The focus shifted completely towards her. The last few months, since she was born, have been very beautiful," he said.With time, the Mumbai batter began to turn his attention back to cricket. Rather than dwell on his international setback, he started looking towards the very things that had fuelled his journey from the beginning. And now, with 113 T20I appearances behind him, he is hoping there is still more to come in India colours."The first two months, though, were very difficult. But then I thought, why not go back to thinking about how I was before?"How I started my cricket all I used to think about was playing age-group cricket for Mumbai and eventually representing Mumbai in First-Class cricket," he said.BACK TO NORMALThe road to rediscovery was not a journey Suryakumar undertook alone. The 36-year-old revealed that a conversation with his wife, Devisha Shetty, proved to be an important turning point. Her advice was simple: go back to the mindset of the teenager who dreamed of representing Mumbai and playing the game he loved."I sat down and thought about all these things and started chatting with my wife. She said the same thing - I needed to bring back the love and passion for the game that I had when I was a 15-year-old kid, who wanted to represent Mumbai in Under-15 cricket," Suryakumar said.That message appears to have struck a chord. Instead of allowing his India setback to define him, Suryakumar has returned to the basics, focusing on training, enjoying the game and finding his competitive edge again."So, that's what I started thinking about, and I am now following the same things I did 10-15 years ago. I am training again, following the same passion and the same love for the game."Everything is back to normal now. When you start thinking about it and focus on playing this sport, you want to do well for your team and your family. Things change completely, and that's what I am doing right now."The main goal is what I used to think about before, win games for Mumbai and win the championship for Mumbai," he added.For Suryakumar, the opportunity to put that renewed mindset into practice is not far away. He is set to lead Mumbai in the upcoming Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, with the domestic T20 competition offering him a platform to make a statement.A strong campaign could put him back in the selectors' conversations, but for now, his immediate focus appears to be much simpler. The man who once dreamed of playing for Mumbai as a 15-year-old is back to chasing that same joy.And perhaps that is the most important first step in his journey back.- Ends

articles.title: Sanju Samson back in Kerala colours, named Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy captain - India Today
articles.summary: Sanju Samson back in Kerala colours, named Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy captain India Today
articles.content: Sanju Samson will return to domestic cricket as Kerala captain, having been entrusted with the leadership role for the 2026 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. The wicketkeeper-batter will lead an 18-member squad in the tournament, which begins on November 24.It will be Samson's first appearance for Kerala since January, when he featured in a Vijay Hazare Trophy fixture against Puducherry. The India opener has since been occupied with national duties, playing an important role in India's successful T20 World Cup title defence and their gold medal-winning campaign at the Asian Games. Samson was part of the Indian team that beat New Zealand in the T20I series 3-2 recently. (Credit: Kerala cricket association X)Kerala will begin their SMAT campaign against Madhya Pradesh at the PCA Stadium in Tira, near Mohali. Both teams are part of Group C, which also features Andhra, Assam, Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra, Puducherry and Tripura.Samson had led Kerala in the previous edition as well, but the team could only manage a fourth-place finish in Elite Group A and failed to progress to the next stage. The wicketkeeper-batter enjoyed a productive campaign individually, accumulating 233 runs from six innings at a strike rate of 137.86. He was Kerala's second-highest run-getter, behind Rohan Kunnummal.The squad features several familiar names, including red-ball captain Vishnu Vinod and former skipper Mohammed Azharuddeen. Experienced spinner Jalaj Saxena, who made his way back into the side ahead of the Ranji Trophy campaign, has also been picked.Kerala have also rewarded promising performers from the Kerala Cricket League, with Ahammed Imran and Govind Dev D. Pai earning places in the squad after consistent performances in the competition.There is also IPL experience in the mix. Vignesh Puthur, who has turned out for Mumbai Indians and Rajasthan Royals, has been included alongside K. M. Asif, who was part of Chennai Super Kings' title-winning squads in 2018 and 2021.KERALA SQUAD FOR SYED MUSHTAQ ALI TROPHYSanju V Samson (C) (WK), Rohan S Kunnummal, Mohammed Azharuddeen (WK), Ahammed Imran, Govind Dev D Pai, Krishna Devan R J, Vishnu Vinod (WK), Salman Nizar, Akhil Scaria, Nikhil M, Vignesh Puthur, Biju Narayanan N, Karthik B Nair, Vaisakh Chandran, Asif K M, Nidheesh M D, Sharafuddeen NM, Jalaj Saxena- Ends

articles.title: Chennai set to bring Asian Athletics Championships back to India in 2029 - India Today
articles.summary: Chennai set to bring Asian Athletics Championships back to India in 2029 India Today
articles.content: Chennai is on the verge of securing the rights to host the 2029 Asian Athletics Championships, with the Asian Athletics Association (AAA) awaiting formal assurances from the Tamil Nadu government before making the award official.The continental body's council discussed the proposal at its 107th meeting in Tokyo on Tuesday. The final confirmation is expected once the state government submits the required financial and administrative guarantees.“Subject to presentation of letters of guarantee from the Govt, Asian Athletics Association is pleased to award the 2029 Asian Athletics Championships to Chennai, Tamil Nadu,” the statement read.C Latha, a senior official of the Tamil Nadu Athletics Association who is in Tokyo as part of the Indian contingent, said the documents were expected to be handed over on Wednesday."We have made the presentation and the Asian Athletics Association (AAA) asked us to submit the financial and other guarantees from the state government. The AAA said they will award the 2029 Asian Championships to Chennai once they get the guarantees," Latha told PTI from Tokyo."We are hoping to get the guarantees tomorrow from our state government. So, the final decision is expected to come tomorrow," she added.World Athletics Vice President and Athletics Federation of India (AFI) spokesperson Adille Sumariwalla was also present at the meeting. He confirmed that Chennai would be awarded the hosting rights once the necessary guarantees were received from the state government.If finalised, the event will mark the third occasion that India has staged the Asian Athletics Championships. Pune hosted the competition in 2013, followed by Bhubaneswar in 2017. Chennai is set to welcome the 28th edition of the biennial event in 2029.The next edition, the 27th in the series, is scheduled to take place in Xiamen, China, between May 28 and June 2, 2027.India is also preparing to stage several major athletics competitions over the coming years. Chandigarh is scheduled to host the Asian Relays Championships in August 2027, while Bhubaneswar will stage both the Asian Indoor Athletics Championships and the World Indoor Athletics Championships in 2028.The country is also in the race to bring the World U20 Athletics Championships to Ahmedabad in 2028.- Ends

articles.title: Owaisi Questions Maharashtra Govt’s UCC Questionnaire - Deccan Chronicle
articles.summary: Owaisi Questions Maharashtra Govt’s UCC Questionnaire Deccan Chronicle
articles.content: Hyderabad: AIMIM President Asaduddin Owaisi has said the Maharashtra government has invited opinions from the public to implement UCC and it has also prepared a questionnaire for it. The questionnaire, prepared by the Maharashtra government, makes it clear that the Devendra Fadnavis government will implement the UCC. The questionnaire consists of leading questions on polygamy and extra-judicial divorce. But there is not one question on Hindu Undivided Family. This makes it evident that, much like the initiatives introduced by BJP governments in Gujarat, Uttarakhand, Assam, and Madhya Pradesh under the guise of a 'Uniform Civil Code,' this is not a true UCC, but rather a 'Hindu Civil Code' that is being imposed upon non-Hindu communities. “Additionally, if you examine the questionnaire, you will find that the majority of the questions are framed in a 'yes or no' format. I believe this is precisely why R.C. Chavan, a retired judge of the Bombay High Court, chose to resign,” he explained. He had stated that there is no one from the minority community. They are talking about implementation in Maharashtra at this juncture, but they are not defining what this 'uniform' actually is."

articles.content: Election to one of Maharashtra’s largest milk federations has turned into a political slugfest. Kolhapur Zilla Sahakari Dudh Utpadak Sangh Ltd, known as Gokul, is one of Maharashtra’s largest and most influential dairy co-operatives. After the election to the directors’ positions was held recently, the Congress-led panel won by a wafer-thin majority of 13-12 in a body of 25 directors. Soon thereafter, the BJP-led State government passed an order to appoint five nominated directors. Four of them will have voting rights. This caused a massive backlash, as it will tilt the majority in favour of the ruling alliance via nominated directors, though the alliance could not garner a majority through a democratically held election. Kolhapur Zilla Sahakari Dudh Utpadak Sangh Ltd., well known for its popular brand ‘Gokul ’, is an Operation Flood cooperative dairy project established on March 16, 1963. It is one of the most significant political and economic forces in western Maharashtra and has established itself as a prime dairy co-operative in the State. Maharashtra’s politics is shaped by the significant co-operatives’ sector.

articles.title: Farmers protest in Kolhapur against Maharashtra government's Gokul board move - The New Indian Express
articles.summary: Farmers protest in Kolhapur against Maharashtra government's Gokul board move The New Indian Express
articles.content: MUMBAI: Thousands of milk-producing farmers took to the streets against the BJP-led Maharashtra government in Kolhapur, protesting and demanding the rescinding of the state government's decision to give voting rights to four directors appointed to the Gokul Milk Federation.Congress leader Satej Patil and farmer leader Raju Shetty organised the massive protest under the banner of the Sangharsh Morcha, where dairy farmers from across Kolhapur district, along with supporters from neighbouring Sangli and Satara, participated in the march at Dasara Chowk in Kolhapur.During the protest, several farmers brought their cattle, underlining their opposition to what they described as government interference in a cooperative institution built around milk producers. Local lawyers also participated, carrying black flags and banners opposing the government's decision.The protest came against the backdrop of the Maharashtra Cabinet's November 4 decision to amend the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, allowing the government to nominate five members to the managing committees of cooperative institutions with an annual turnover exceeding Rs 500 crore.Of the five nominees, four will have voting rights, while the fifth will be a government officer not below the rank of assistant registrar without voting rights. The nominated members, however, will not be eligible to contest elections for office-bearer posts..Bombay HC refuses to stay Gokul Chairman polls; four govt-nominated directors allowed to cast votes.The government's decision has triggered a major controversy because of the recent Gokul board elections held on October 19. The Congress-led Samvichari Aghadi won 13 of the 25 seats, while the BJP-led Mahayuti panel secured 12. The outcome gave the opposition-backed panel a narrow majority in the influential dairy cooperative, which has an annual turnover of more than Rs 4,000 crore.Opposition leaders allege that the government has introduced the amendment to alter the electoral arithmetic after the Mahayuti failed to secure a majority. With four government-nominated members enjoying voting rights, the ruling alliance could potentially increase its strength from 12 to 16, against the 13 elected Congress-led panel directors.The Opposition alleged that the state government's decision was an attempt to overturn the mandate of nearly 5.5 lakh milk producers represented through the cooperative's electoral process.The controversy intensified after the election of Gokul's chairman was stalled because of a lack of quorum. Under the cooperative's bylaws, at least 14 directors are required to be present for the chairman's election. The 12 Mahayuti-backed directors remained absent from the earlier meeting, preventing the 13-member opposition-backed group from completing the process.Meanwhile, the Bombay High Court refused to stay the state government's decision and allowed the election of Gokul chairman on November 10, 2026. The court asked that the votes of state government-appointed directors be kept in a sealed cover. The entire election process must also be video-recorded. The election result will be declared, but its validity will remain subject to the final outcome of the court proceedings scheduled for November 25..Gokul takeover row: Maharashtra move to appoint five directors sparks political clash.Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

articles.contentMarathi: MUMBAI: Thousands of milk-producing farmers took to the streets against the BJP-led Maharashtra government in Kolhapur, protesting and demanding the rescinding of the state government's decision to give voting rights to four directors appointed to the Gokul Milk Federation.Congress leader Satej Patil and farmer leader Raju Shetty organised the massive protest under the banner of the Sangharsh Morcha, where dairy farmers from across Kolhapur district, along with supporters from neighbouring Sangli and Satara, participated in the march at Dasara Chowk in Kolhapur.During the protest, several farmers brought their cattle, underlining their opposition to what they described as government interference in a cooperative institution built around milk producers. Local lawyers also participated, carrying black flags and banners opposing the government's decision.The protest came against the backdrop of the Maharashtra Cabinet's November 4 decision to amend the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, allowing the government to nominate five members to the managing committees of cooperative institutions with an annual turnover exceeding Rs 500 crore.Of the five nominees, four will have voting rights, while the fifth will be a government officer not below the rank of assistant registrar without voting rights. The nominated members, however, will not be eligible to contest elections for office-bearer posts..Bombay HC refuses to stay Gokul Chairman polls; four govt-nominated directors allowed to cast votes.The government's decision has triggered a major controversy because of the recent Gokul board elections held on October 19. The Congress-led Samvichari Aghadi won 13 of the 25 seats, while the BJP-led Mahayuti panel secured 12. The outcome gave the opposition-backed panel a narrow majority in the influential dairy cooperative, which has an annual turnover of more than Rs 4,000 crore.Opposition leaders allege that the government has introduced the amendment to alter the electoral arithmetic after the Mahayuti failed to secure a majority. With four government-nominated members enjoying voting rights, the ruling alliance could potentially increase its strength from 12 to 16, against the 13 elected Congress-led panel directors.The Opposition alleged that the state government's decision was an attempt to overturn the mandate of nearly 5.5 lakh milk producers represented through the cooperative's electoral process.The controversy intensified after the election of Gokul's chairman was stalled because of a lack of quorum. Under the cooperative's bylaws, at least 14 directors are required to be present for the chairman's election. The 12 Mahayuti-backed directors remained absent from the earlier meeting, preventing the 13-member opposition-backed group from completing the process.Meanwhile, the Bombay High Court refused to stay the state government's decision and allowed the election of Gokul chairman on November 10, 2026. The court asked that the votes of state government-appointed directors be kept in a sealed cover. The entire election process must also be video-recorded. The election result will be declared, but its validity will remain subject to the final outcome of the court proceedings scheduled for November 25..Gokul takeover row: Maharashtra move to appoint five directors sparks political clash.Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

articles.title: Indian sports wrap, November 9: Schedule announced for KIYG 2026; Atiqa Mir shines on FIA Worlds debut - Sportstar
articles.summary: Indian sports wrap, November 9: Schedule announced for KIYG 2026; Atiqa Mir shines on FIA Worlds debut Sportstar
articles.content: Chennai MORE SPORTS Hyderabad to stage 22 of 27 competitive sports as softball debuts and sailing features as a demonstration event Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya on Monday announced the full schedule of the Khelo India Youth Games 2026, to be hosted by Telangana from December 11-22. The Games will feature 27 competitive sports and one demonstration sport. Venues in Hyderabad, including the Lal Bahadur Shastri Stadium complex and the Gachibowli sports complex, will stage 22 sports. The rest will be held in Khammam (archery), Hanumankonda (athletics), Karimnagar (judo), Nizamabad (table tennis) and Mahbubnagar (kabaddi). Around 6,000 athletes and 1,800 support staff are expected at the 12-day event, the first Khelo India event hosted by Telangana. Softball debuts as a competitive sport, while sailing makes its first appearance as a demonstration event. “I am very excited to announce the schedule of Khelo India Youth Games 2026,” said Dr Mandaviya. “Since KIYG are coming at the back of the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, we can expect to see some quality performances.” In the previous edition in Bihar, Maharashtra topped the table with 58 gold medals for its fifth title, ahead of Haryana and Rajasthan. -Team Sportstar YOUTH OLYMPICS India’s lone archer at the Youth Olympics, Gatha Khadake, bowed out of the women’s individual recurve U-18 competition after losing a shoot-off to sixth seed Yeeun Whang of the USA in a closely fought quarterfinal in Dakar on Monday. After a gruelling five-set contest ended 5-5, Gatha lost 5-6 (9-9) with both archers scoring nine, but Whang prevailed as her arrow was closer to the centre of the target. - PTI MOTORSPORTS Atiqa Mir produces overtaking masterclass to finish 6th on FIA World Championship debut Indian racing prodigy Atiqa Mir made a stunning recovery on her FIA Karting World Championship debut, climbing 16 places to finish sixth in Race 1. The 11-year-old, the first Indian backed by the Formula 1 Academy, races in the 12-14 category for Kart Republic. Her P6 was the best by an Indian this weekend. Two crashed drivers blocked her hot lap in qualifying, leaving her 83rd of 87. With three heats to recover, she gained 16 places in Race 1, 10 in Race 2 and four in Race 3, finishing 40th overall. In the Super Heat, she started 14th, but a crash dropped her to P16. “That was a lot of fun and I got amazing overtaking practice, that is how I treated this weekend after the qualifying disaster. That was out of my control so I took control of what I could and drove my heart out.” “I feel I belong at this level and with a better qualifying, I can fight at the front. I want to thank my sponsors Raise and JK Tyre without whom none of this won’t be possible” said Atiqa. Her father Asif Mir, India’s first national karting champion, said, “We were looking really strong for a top five result but the qualifying spoilt everything for her. (It was) such a shame as she (had) worked really hard to get up to pace. But what followed surprised even me. She is a gutsy little girl playing with the big boys, I was very impressed.” -Team Sportstar TENNIS TPL to award scholarships to 36 juniors, U-14 champs to earn Road to Australian Open 2027 opportunity The Tennis Premier League (TPL) has announced the dates for the 2026 Race to Gold (RTG) Masters, a grassroots initiative that will see 36 promising junior tennis players from six states — Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Telangana and Karnataka, along with the North Zone — receive scholarships. Two U-14 champions will also earn the opportunity to travel to the Australian Open 2027. The six U-14 boys’ and six U-14 girls’ scholarship winners from the six regions will compete in a final round-robin tournament in Mumbai on November 29. The top boy and girl from this event will each earn the opportunity to travel to Melbourne. - Team Sportstar
